rationale: Anchors Locard's principle precisely after its content block — tests the canonical formulation which students must be able to recite and apply.
Tests preservative selection — specifically the EDTA tube for DNA (not NaF) and the formalin-trap for viscera — after the collection and preservation content block.
Tests the chain of custody rule — a break renders evidence inadmissible — after the custody content block.
Tests the fundamental role distinction between the forensic physician as a witness to facts — not as an advocate — after the legal and professional context content block.
Tests applied reasoning on translating findings into opinion and the 'findings vs opinion' fault line after the interpretation content block.
Tests the Selvi v Karnataka 2010 ruling — polygraph/narcoanalysis inadmissible as evidence — immediately after the lie-detection content block. Critical accuracy point.
Tests the STR method as the standard for DNA profiling immediately after the DNA profiling content block — a basic but frequently confused fact.
Tests the Section 65B certificate requirement for electronic evidence — the most commonly forgotten step in digital forensics — after the cyber forensics content block.
Tests the privacy framework governing medical records and the doctor's disclosure obligations after the privacy legal framework content block.
Tests the blood grouping procedure — EDTA tube for DNA collection, correct Landsteiner's Law application, tile method — after the practical technique content block.
Tests the air-dry-before-sealing DNA exhibit rule — the single most important DNA collection step — after the applied practice and chain-of-custody content block.
